answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after posting a bond that is slashed if later evidence links their account to coordinated fraud. A ridge of independent witnesses must attest to each newcomer, and their bonds are also at risk if they knowingly vouch for a sybil. This makes identities costly to multiply: an attacker must lock up capital across many accounts and risk losing it, rather than merely minting usernames. On a velvet terrace of low-stakes discussion, the bond can stay small; high-impact decisions require more collateral.
